title: Check the engine version at client startup
summary: Whenever the client is about to call the engine, it first verifies the engine: a missing engine produces a message that names the engine and the concrete install command, an engine below the declared minimum produces a message that names the required version and the concrete upgrade command, and a compatible engine proceeds normally. Reporting the client's own version and the declared requirement is exempt from this check and works without an engine, so a bare `executable not found` failure is never the outcome of a command that needs the engine.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

checks.criterion: With no engine installed, the version report exits successfully and prints the client version and the declared minimum engine version.
With no engine installed, usage help exits successfully and is printed.
With no engine installed, an operation that needs the engine fails non-zero with a message naming the engine and a runnable install instruction.
With an engine below the declared minimum, an operation that needs the engine fails non-zero naming the required version, the version found and a runnable upgrade instruction.
An engine that answers without a usable version is reported like a too-old engine and the operation does nothing through the engine.
An engine at or above the declared minimum is used with unchanged requests, output and exit status.
Numeric comparison accepts 0.10.0 against a 0.9.0 minimum, accepts equality with the minimum, and ignores non-numeric suffixes.
The engine's version is requested at most once per invocation and a failed confirmation leaves the engine with no request from the operation.
In the machine-readable output form, the missing-engine and too-old-engine failures each yield exactly one failure result with the same message and a non-zero exit.
Starting the interactive session with no engine prints the install guidance and exits non-zero instead of opening a prompt.
The minimum engine version printed by the version report and the one enforced before use are identical.
The install and upgrade instructions in the failure messages are concrete and can be pasted and run as printed.
